claims.statement: For the five specified rooted claw-branch trees with branch-length lists [1,1,2], [1,1,3], [1,2,3], [1,1,2,3], and [1,1,2,4], at p=x(T)+2, the literal fixed-selector weighted network with all deletion and exact two-for-one switch arcs has an integral flow saturating all upper supply; each corresponding complete aggregate is negative.
claims.scope: Exactly those five trees and tested ranks, reconstructed from the recipes and edge lists in evidence.json. This is a bounded result, not the universal ordinary-tree claim or a generation-complete family.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: copied-source replay confirms all five exact selectors, complete sums, capacities, legal move networks, and saturated integer flows. The universal quantifier over all ordinary trees and all eligible p is unsupported; no supplied or replayed counterexample refutes it. Saturation implies the scalar inequality on these rows, while the universal flow claim is a stronger sufficient mechanism.

limitations: Only five hand-selected trees were replayed; no exhaustive tree generation or universal argument is supplied.
Every leaf in the five cases is favorable, and only p=x+2 was tested.
The stronger universal weighted-flow mechanism remains open; a deficient flow cut alone would not refute the scalar aggregate.
